briefing.headline: US-China AI chip export controls tighten as o4 and Claude 4 race toward agentic capabilities

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: Frontier labs accelerate multi-agent systems while governments impose stricter export controls. Funding remains robust with focus on inference infrastructure and safety tooling.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI released o4-preview with advanced tool-use chaining. Anthropic's Claude 4 Opus shows gains in long-horizon planning. Meta open-sourced Llama 4 405B weights under new safety license.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems and that DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level. New NIST guidelines target agentic workflow risks.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: TSMC begins volume production of 2nm AI chips. Microsoft announces $15B Texas data center expansion for OpenAI workloads. Google TPU v6 pods reach 100k-chip scale.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will multi-agent coordination protocols become the decisive moat or will open standards erode first-mover advantages?
